svg.text: Mix 'n Smash carrier board: ESP32-DevKitC (38 pins)
Perfboard 7 × 9 cm, 24 × 30 holes. Columns A–X, rows 1–30. Red = +5 V, dark blue = GND, orange = ESP32 5 V after the diode, grey = other bare links. Thin coloured lines = insulated wire.
Thick bare lines: tinned copper wire on the solder side (the two short links in column X carry the strip current: 0.8–1 mm wire). Short grey bars: solder bridges between neighbouring holes.
R1 330 Ω · R2 1 kΩ · R3 100 kΩ
1. Mount the ESP32 with its USB connector to the right (column W side), as drawn. The other way round fits too, but puts 5 V on the wrong pins: mark the board.
2. H2 (row 3) only holds the ESP32, except the GPIO 16 pin, which carries the strip data. On a 1-inch wide devkit H2 goes in row 2: solder both headers with the ESP32 plugged in.
3. D1 (stripe towards the ESP32) feeds the ESP32 from the 5 V supply but blocks the other way: a USB cable alone can no longer power the strip.
4. R2 limits the current into U1 while the strip is unpowered; R3 keeps the data line low while the ESP32 boots, so the strip does not flicker.
5. Without U1: put a wire link in the socket from pin 2 to pin 3. R1 and R2 then sit in series in the data line, which is fine.
6. J2: check with a continuity tester that header pin 1 really goes to RJ45 contact 1. Label the socket "no network": PoE switches put up to 48 V on these pins.
7. Insulated wires may cross anything. Keep them away from the area under the ESP32 antenna (left end) where you can.
E25 → K15: +5V for the button lights
L26 → X21: strip data to the terminal
